full_judgment:
In this Rule the petitioner has challenged the concurrent decisions of both the courts below in allowing a pre-emption case under section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act. There was no dispute with regard to the limitation and or defect of parties as such. The pre-emption is being claimed by two co-sharers of the same suit holding, both of them claiming under one Nepal Sarker. One Rahimuddin Sarker and Mazharul Hannan claimed pre-emption alleging to be co-sharers by inheritance being the grand-children of one Amirullah Sarker who became the co-sharer in the suit holding by purchase. One of the pre-emptees Rafiqul Alam also claimed pre-emption and made himself added as a co-pre-emptor along with the original pre-emptors. Rafiqul Alarn claimed to be a co-sharer by purchase. There is no dispute with regard to the fact that both Rahimuddin Sarker and Mazharul Hannan on the one hand and Rafiqul Alam on the other hand were co-sharers in the suit holding at the time when the impugned transfer was made and the pre-emption case was filed. It is also admitted the Rahimuddin Sarkar and Mazharul Hannan inherited through their father who inherited through their grand-father. It is also not disputed that Rafiqul Alam became a co-sharer by his own purchase. So the admitted fact remains that both the contending pre-emptors are co-sharers. 

 2. The main and only question that arises for decision in this case is as to what be the priority in between the co-sharers inter se over the claim of pre-emption, i.e., as a co-sharer by inheritance an a co-sharer, by purchase who would get first preference over the claim of pre-emption. The answer to this question lies exclusively in the explicit language of clause (a) of sub-section (5) of section 96 of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act; it says that if a co-sharer tenant whose interest has accrued by inheritance and a co-Sharer tenant whose interest has accrued by purchase and a tenant holding land contiguous to the land transferred apply for pre-emption, such applicant shall have the prior right to purchase in the order in which they have been mentioned hereinabove. From the aforesaid provisions of law it clearly appeals that the legislature has fixed the priority between co-sharers by inheritance and purchase and contiguous owners and that a co-sharer by inheritance has the highest priority to claim pre-emption in any holding in question.
